about.title: Isleton Slip & Fall & Premises Liability Claims
about.longDescription: Isleton is a small Sacramento County town, and many of its buildings, sidewalks, and businesses sit near the Delta along SR-160, H Street, and Isleton Road. A wet floor at a local market, a broken step outside a historic building, or a poorly lit walkway near the river can cause a serious fall in an instant. Because Isleton is small, evidence like surveillance footage or incident reports may not be kept long, so acting quickly matters. California law requires showing the property owner knew or reasonably should have known about the hazard and failed to address it. LawProactive doesn't practice law ourselves — we're a free service that connects you with an independent attorney familiar with these claims. They can help you gather photos, witness information, and records while the details are still fresh, and explain how comparative fault might apply to your specific fall.
about.ctaText: Talk to an independent attorney about your fall — free, no obligation.

items.title: Notice Is Everything in These Cases
items.desc: California requires showing the property owner knew or should have known about the hazard and didn't fix or warn about it. An attorney can help identify what evidence supports that notice before it disappears.

items.title: Video and Records Don't Wait
items.desc: Surveillance footage at small businesses is often overwritten within days or weeks. Connecting quickly with an attorney can help preserve footage and incident reports tied to your fall.

items.title: Comparative Fault Doesn't Bar Your Claim
items.desc: Even if you're partly responsible for a fall, California's pure comparative fault rule allows you to still recover a share of damages. An attorney can walk you through how this might apply to your situation.

items.question: How long do I have to file a slip and fall claim in Isleton?
items.answer: Generally, California gives you two years from the date of the fall to file a premises liability lawsuit. If a public entity owned or maintained the property, that window is much shorter and requires an early claim. An attorney can confirm the deadline that applies to your situation.

items.question: What if the store or property owner says I wasn't paying attention?
items.answer: California's pure comparative fault rule means you can still recover damages even if you're found partly at fault, though your share of responsibility may reduce the amount. This is common in these cases and doesn't automatically end a claim. An independent attorney can help evaluate the specific facts.

items.question: Isleton is a small town — will a business really have security footage?
items.answer: Some Isleton businesses along SR-160 or H Street have cameras, but recordings are often kept for only a short time before being erased. That's why documenting the hazard with photos and getting contact information from witnesses right away is so important. An attorney can also send a preservation request to the business quickly.
